subject: Analysis reccomendations based on sampling design?

messages.author: 9f3eb94af51eff72
messages.subject: Analysis reccomendations based on sampling design?
parts:
Hello all,

I would appreciate a bit of direction:
I have a data set that includes 3 years of point count data, but am struggling with how to decide the best way to analyze it. The faculty in my department cannot/will not offer any helpful guidance. Very thankful for this group!

Here is the structure of my data:
  • 28 point count stations (250 meter radius; each point separated by 500m to avoid overlap)
    • We spatially distributed the listening stations (as best we could) to get 7 in each of 4 major cover types (these can/will be reworked to be continuous habitat covariates instead of 4 categories)
  • 3 seasons (years; no hypotheses about differences between years in habitat config., mgmt, etc.)
  • 3 visits per season (sometimes only 2 visits due to inclement weather)
  • Detections of several passerine spp. recorded to nearest meter and azimuth (I don't mind binning these into any number of discrete distance bands; the first detection only of each individual; successive vocalizations were ignored when it could be reasonable assumed it was the same individual)
  • We also recorded covariates that might affect detection rates (cloud cover, time since sunrise, et al. applicable data)
I understand the need to model each spp. separately, etc. with best fitting key fxns.
Q1: What I am mainly struggling with is the small myriad of ways to frame the data and subsequently analyze it. Can somebody recommend the "best" way to proceed? We are interested in density if possible, but realize that occupancy may be the fallback due to our medium-small sample size. I have played with these basic tutorials (https://darinjmcneil.weebly.com/), but find myself wishing the tutorials explained things a bit better...
Q2: How do you set up the analyses to incorporate separate years as well as the multiple visits/station?

I would greatly appreciate any advice or examples that closely mirror my sampling design. My main problem is that I absolutely love nitty gritty details of analyses, but I cannot help but overwhelm myself when it comes to making a final decision on which one to apply. I see too many viable options and no vignette I have found "looks like" my data.

Many thanks!
DM
